Chapter 10: The Ongoing Work of Reclaiming Language and Power
The journey doesn’t really end with just one word, or one bold act. Reclaiming language and power—it’s not a box you check off. It’s an ongoing practice, something that unfolds over a lifetime. It’s about showing up for yourself, again and again, even when it feels tough.
There are days when that old shame sneaks back in, when the world feels just a bit heavier, and the fight ahead seems endless. But then, there are also days filled with joy, moments of connection, and those tiny breakthroughs that remind you why you keep going. Every moment gives you a choice—to speak up, to reach out, to keep moving forward.
Picture this: a group of women comes together for a workshop. They’re swapping stories, sharing strategies for living boldly. They talk about the words that once hurt them, and the words they’ve taken back as their own. There’s a real power in naming things—calling out injustice, voicing their desires, and claiming their stories.
Most people don’t realize just how much power lives inside our language. The words we use shape how we see ourselves, and how others see us too. When women reclaim the words that have been used against them, they’re not just changing their own story—they’re changing it for everyone.
This work? It’s never really finished. There will always be fresh challenges, new battles, and more words to reclaim. But with every step, the path gets a little easier. The community grows stronger, and the sense of what’s possible keeps expanding.
Independence isn’t a finish line. It’s a practice—a willingness to keep trying, keep learning, and keep loving. It takes courage to show up, to speak out, to really live.
And as the journey goes on, one truth stands out: the power to define your own life is yours, and yours alone. No one can take that away from you. No one else gets to tell you who you are. That’s your birthright, your inheritance—your own declaration of independence.
